enumeration.title: Continuing a list
enumeration.text: Etcétera stands for further items that are understood from the list. It is usually abbreviated etc.; it does not agree with the listed nouns.

noun-m.title: Masculine noun
noun-m.text: This entry is masculine in the sense shown. Its usual definite article is el; plural nouns use los. Grammatical gender is a property of the noun, not a rule about the thing it names.

noun-f.title: Feminine noun
noun-f.text: This entry is feminine in the sense shown. Its usual definite article is la; plural nouns use las. Learn the gender with the word rather than guessing from its ending.

noun-mf.title: Gender in context
noun-mf.text: This noun can be masculine or feminine. The forms and usage note distinguish the relevant meanings or uses; do not choose a gender from the spelling alone.

infinitive.title: Infinitive
infinitive.text: The headword is an infinitive: the dictionary form of a verb. A finite form changes with person and tense. An infinitive can follow another verb or a preposition; the particular construction determines which preposition, if any, is needed.

adjective.title: Adjective agreement
adjective.text: An adjective describes or classifies a noun and agrees with it in gender and number. Some adjectives have the same masculine and feminine form. The listed forms are not different vocabulary items.

adverb.title: Adverb
adverb.text: An adverb modifies a verb, adjective, another adverb or a whole statement. In this grammatical use it does not agree with a noun in gender or number.

preposition.title: Preposition
preposition.text: A preposition introduces a complement and expresses a relation to the rest of the phrase. Its English translation depends on the construction; learn it with the words around it.

conjunction.title: Conjunction
conjunction.text: A conjunction links words, phrases or clauses. Its role and English translation depend on what it connects.

pronoun.title: Pronoun
pronoun.text: A pronoun stands for a person, thing or idea. Subject, object and prepositional forms have different jobs; the usage note identifies the form taught here.

relative.title: Relative word
relative.text: A relative word introduces a clause that relates to a noun or other antecedent. Relative forms normally lack the written accent used in corresponding question words.

question.title: Question or exclamation
question.text: This accented form is used in direct and indirect questions or exclamations. Keep the written accent; an unaccented spelling can have a different grammatical role.

quantifier.title: Quantity
quantifier.text: A quantifier expresses an amount, number or extent. Its position and any agreement depend on the particular word and use; do not assume all quantifiers change in the same way.

possessive.title: Possessive
possessive.text: Possessive forms identify an owner. Forms that vary agree with the thing owned, rather than with the owner. Some have short forms before a noun and longer forms elsewhere.

demonstrative.title: Demonstrative
demonstrative.text: A demonstrative points to something in the physical or conversational context. Forms used with a noun agree with it; neuter forms stand on their own.

number.title: Number word
number.text: This card teaches a numerical use. Cardinal numbers count, while ordinals identify a position in a sequence. Agreement depends on the particular number word.

article.title: Article
article.text: An article belongs with a noun. Its form normally agrees with the noun’s gender and number.
